target_customer: E-commerce retailers and sellers of virtual goods wanting to personalize pricing and discounts
problem: Retailers handed out blanket promo codes that cut margin. Freshplum used models to offer personalized discounts only to shoppers who looked unlikely to buy otherwise.
business_model: B2B SaaS and API embedded by JavaScript on retailer sites
product_category: E-commerce personalization, pricing and promotions analytics

founders.name: Sam Odio
previous_startups: Divvyshot (photo sharing, acquired by Facebook in 2010)
founders.background_notes: TNW June 2012 and YC page; the YC page says he scaled products to 500M plus users.

founders.name: Nick Alexander
previous_startups: An earlier online business that Odio later handed to him (per TNW 2012, unnamed)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as founder and CTO without a bio.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed machine learning models scoring shoppers in real time at over 10 million API requests a day in alpha, with easy JavaScript embedding.

defensibility.rationale: Models could improve with merchant data, but the approach was copyable by personalization and retargeting vendors, and the company stayed small.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TellApart bought Freshplum in July 2014 to add personalized discounts to its retargeting.

market_need_then: Retailers lost margin to public promo codes; the founders pitched models as a scalpel against a sledgehammer and the 2012 launch was backed by Google Ventures, NEA and Greylock.

branding.domain_note: freshplum.com now redirects to a GoDaddy for sale page, so the domain was dropped after the acquisition.

brand_strength.rationale: No evidence of brand identity, mascot or community; only trade press covering the product and founders' Facebook background.

outcome_analysis: Freshplum launched out of stealth in June 2012 with a 1.4 million dollar seed from NEA, Greylock, Google Ventures and CRV, added about 1 million dollars in 2014 and was bought by TellApart in July 2014 for an undisclosed sum, giving seed backers an exit. The team had prior exit experience at Divvyshot, and the outcome looks like a technology acquisition of a small team rather than a breakout.
notes: freshplum.com redirects to a domain for sale page (site dead). The February 2014 round of 1 million is from one outlet (Global Venturing) and stage is not stated, so recorded as other; a search snippet cited TechCrunch as saying over 2.5 million raised in total, which may include this. Seed amount confirmed by TNW and echoed by Global Venturing. Michael Yuan is named as cofounder in TNW and press snippets but the YC page lists only two founders, so not recorded as a founder. Founders' education and prior employers other than Facebook not found; Facebook employment of Odio is from press snippet wording about ex-Facebook executives and TNW's Divvyshot mention. No competitors dated near the batch found; TNW 2012 named none. Name origin search returned only unrelated plum brands.
